newsitem.title: SLOVAKIA: EU hands Slovakia list of membership conditions.
newsitem.headline: EU hands Slovakia list of membership conditions.

text.p: The European Union expressed concern on Thursday over the slow pace of democratic reforms in Slovakia and presented it with a list of conditions that Bratislava must still fulfil to gain EU membership.

But EU External Relations Commissioner Hans van den Broek, visiting the country ahead of a final assessment next month of Slovakia's eligibility to join the bloc, said there was no danger of the EU cancelling Slovakia's association agreement.
"We both agreed there were stronger and weaker points," van den Broek said after meeting Prime Minister Vladimir Meciar. "Our discussion was very lengthy, thorough and frank."

EU officials have said they were worried by events surrounding referendums last weekends on NATO membership and direct presidential elections that were declared void because ballot papers were invalid.
"It is quite clear that we have noted with concern the events of the past week," Van den Broek said after meeting Deputy Foreign Minister Jozef Sestak.
"We want to clarify and discuss very openly but we want to make clear we are not biased," he said, adding the community wanted Slovakia to be part of the European family.
Meciar himself did not comment on the talks, but his spokeswoman, Magda Pospisilova, said he had conceded many points of criticism of Slovakia's current political scene.
"Both sides agreed that that there is much to be desired as regards political pluralism and political culture in Slovakia," she said.

The twinned referendums were billed as a last chance for Slovakia, which has come under fire from the West for its lack of democratic reforms, to win an invitation to join the North Atlantic Treaty Organisation in the first wave of new members.

Instead, voting degenerated into chaos because of a feud between Prime Minister Vladimir Meciar and President Michal Kovac, who wanted a question about presidential elections on the ballot and prompted a boycott when it was struck off at the last moment.
The Central Referendum Committee declared the widely boycotted weekend referendum void and denounced ballot papers distributed by the Interior Ministry as a "massive swindle".
Van den Broek said that his mission was to clarify points of economic and political questions which are needed for fullfilment of criteria for EU membership.
"This is an important part in time on our discussions as the commission is preparing a report on the preparedness of candidate members," he said.
Sestak was representing the foreign ministry following the resignation last Monday of Foreign Minister Pavol Hamzik .
